passage:
Tariq stayed quiet in the car home from his cousin's flat. A grown-up there had touched him in a way that felt wrong and said, "Don't tell." His stomach hurt and he could not work out why he felt so scared. At home he tried to tell Dad, but Dad was on a work call and said, "Later, buddy."
Next morning he found his teacher, Liam, and whispered, "Someone said not to tell."
Liam knelt down and listened without hurrying. "Thank you for telling me. It is never your fault. I will stay with you, and we will go to the head teacher together, right now."

qa.q: Who did Tariq try to tell first when he got home?
How did Tariq feel after the grown-up said don't tell?
qa.a: He was frightened and confused: his stomach hurt and he could not work out why he felt so scared.

qa.q: What did Liam do that helped Tariq?
qa.a: Liam knelt down, listened without hurrying, said it is never Tariq's fault, stayed with him and took him to the head teacher straight away. 🤍

qa.q: What might it have been like for Tariq when Dad said later?
qa.a: He may have felt he could not get the words out or that no one would listen, yet he kept trying with another grown-up the next day.

grounding: A child touched wrongly and told not to tell feels frightened and confused; he keeps telling until a trusted grown-up helps.
